output.brief: Please don't send the breach notice. The evidence points away from Tessaly's crews and toward the tag stock change on 1 September. Pelion moved to the same Tessaly crew pool on the same day, and its rate didn't change (3.6–3.8). Corvane's bags that were read automatically stayed at about 3.8–3.9. The whole rise sits in bags diverted to the manual encode desk (0.2 to about 4 per 1,000). Of those bags, 91% reached the lateral after it closed. The tags failing to read are the ones printed on the new Fennick stock at Harlow Bay (11.8% no-read, against about 1.5% before). The same counters printing on old Brackwater stock on 14–16 Oct failed at 1.6%, while kiosks on Fennick failed at 12.1% on the same days. The reader arrays are not at fault. The added evening flights don't explain it either. What we don't yet know is whether the Fennick media is itself defective or the printers' heat settings were never adjusted for it. I'm quite sure of the main finding. I'm less sure about the printer-jam link. Next steps: switch back to Brackwater stock now (about five weeks are in stores), and check the result against the no-read rate. Ask HBAA for an extra encode workstation in the evening as a stopgap. Test the Fennick stock and printer settings (see the Teyra bulletin) before lodging any claim with Fennick. Hold the Tessaly penalty.
